About Us

At Red Fox Remodeling, we believe your home should be designed around the way you live. As a locally owned and operated remodeling company serving the Twin Cities, we specialize in creating thoughtful, beautifully crafted spaces that feel as functional as they are inviting.

​

Whether it's a kitchen where family gathers, a bathroom that offers a daily retreat, or a whole-home transformation, we approach every project with care, clear communication, and a commitment to quality. Our team works closely with homeowners from the first conversation through the final walkthrough, ensuring every detail reflects your vision and lifestyle.

​

We take pride in delivering exceptional craftsmanship, using premium materials, and building lasting relationships with the families we serve. For us, remodeling is about more than improving homes, it's about creating spaces where life's best moments unfold.

Meet Your Team
Denny Meints

Owner + Operations

Denny Meints is the founder of Red Fox Remodeling. He started the company in 2022 after years of experience in home remodeling and construction management. Denny built Red Fox around integrity, transparent pricing, and quality craftsmanship. Today, he leads a team serving Twin Cities homeowners and transforming houses into homes.

Asher Webb

Project Manager

Asher has worked in building and remodeling industry for over a decade, including five years in executive-level project management. He brings knowledge of the building process, trade management, and client success. His track record and expertise help ensure homeowners receive guidance and a remodeling experience from start to finish.

Wade Kyllonen

Site Supervisor

Wade has spent over 14 years in the remodeling industry, serving clients in the Twin Cities area. He brings a steady presence to job sites and takes pride in keeping projects on time, on budget, and moving smoothly. His experience makes him a great part of the team. Outside of work, Wade enjoys spending time with his family and exploring the outdoors.

Evan Wrazidlo

Carpenter

Evan joins Red Fox as an carpenter, craftsman, and laborer with a passion for quality workmanship. His attention to detail, work ethic, and commitment to construction make him a valuable asset to the team. Evan takes pride in delivering craftsmanship that helps bring each remodeling project to life.

Chad Torp

Construction Estimator

Chad has over 10 years of experience in remodeling as a carpenter, project manager, and construction estimator. He enjoys preparing clients and projects for a successful start and brings a thoughtful, detail-oriented approach to every project. Outside of work, Chad enjoys spending time with his family, hiking, camping, and exploring the outdoors.

Mai See Thao

Lead Designer

Mai See Thao is an interior designer with 7 years of experience creating spaces. She enjoys collaborating with clients to design homes that reflect their lifestyles and personalities. Outside of work, Mai See loves hiking with her dogs, playing pickleball, and hosting friends. She values relationships with clients and partners.

Graycen Mourhess

Junior Designer

Graycen is a Junior Designer who earned her degree in Interior Design and is excited to begin her remodeling career. She is passionate about creating beautiful, functional spaces that reflect client's style and needs. Graycen enjoys collaborating with clients, bringing ideas to projects, and continuously learning while developing design solutions.

Your Dream Kitchen Built For Your Family

Experience quality craftsmanship with award-winning kitchen remodelers.

Book Your Consultation
Time for a renovation?

We transform kitchens into beautiful, functional spaces that fit your lifestyle. With expert craftsmanship, attention to detail, and a commitment to quality, we deliver remodels that not only look amazing but stand the test of time.

Kitchens Starting at $75k

With every project thoughtfully designed around your vision, needs, and investment. We provide transparent pricing throughout the process, so you always know where your project stands from start to finish.

Increased property value
Modern and customized space
Improved functionality
Fast and efficient build timeline
Entertainment-ready space
Here's how it works:

We turn your vision into reality with transparency, quality assurance, and customer satisfaction at every step.

1. Discovery & Design

We learn about your vision and budget, create your initial design and estimate, and finalize your project direction through a collaborative design and approval process.

2. Prepare & Plan

Our team handles permits, coordinates partners, and sources all materials to ensure everything is ready before construction begins.

3. Build & Celebrate

We bring your project to life with clear communication, walkthroughs, and final touch-ups before celebrating your beautifully finished space.

Frequently Asked Questions
How much will our project cost?

Every kitchen remodel is unique, and the final investment depends on the scope, design, materials, and selections involved. As a general guide, kitchen remodels typically range from $90,000 to $200,000, with projects starting around $75,000 for a more basic scope.

How long does a typical kitchen remodel take?

Most full kitchen remodels take 10 weeks of construction, depending on scope. The entire process including design, selections, permits, and ordering materials often takes 6-8 months from first consultation to completion.

Can I live in my home during the remodel?

In most cases, yes, you can continue to live in your home. You may need to move out of your home for a portion of a kitchen remodel depending on the scope of the project.

How far in advance should I start planning?

Ideally, 3-6 months before you want construction to begin. Custom cabinetry and specialty materials can have long lead times and it's important to leave time for a full custom design process.

Frequently Asked Questions
Is it better to add on to a home or finish existing space like a basement or attic?

We can't say one is better than the other, but utilizing existing space can be a more economical way to gain living space in your home. However, there are plenty of reasons an addition will be a better project to achieve the goals you have for your home!

Do you allow homeowners to contract you for 'partial projects' like only the structural elements?

We will consider a partial project, but there needs to be clear scope delineation from day one and we cannot hand off any work that requires a city inspection connected to our permit. 

Do we need to hire an architect before starting to work with Red Fox?

Do we need to hire an architect before starting to work with Red Fox?

What is a reasonable timeline to expect our addition to be completed in?

Every timeline is unique to the specific project scope, but generally we'll need nine to twelve weeks to design your new space, four to six weeks for project preparations and the build may take anywhere from four to eight months depending on size and scope.

Are you ready for a space you're proud of?

A whole-home remodel gives you the opportunity to completely reimagine the space you already love. From updated layouts and modern finishes to improved functionality and timeless design, we bring every room together into a home that feels beautifully and uniquely yours.

Whole Home Remodels Starting at $350k

For a complete transformation, we thoughtfully reimagine every space in your home to create a cohesive design that fits the way you live. From major structural changes to the finishing details, our team brings your vision to life from start to finish.

Increased property value
Modern and customized space
Better layouts for family time

Here's how it works

We turn your vision into reality with transparency, quality assurance, and customer satisfaction at every step.

1. Discovery & Design

We learn about your vision and budget, create your initial design and estimate, and finalize your project direction through a collaborative design and approval process.

2. Prepare & Plan

Our team handles permits, coordinates partners, and sources all materials to ensure everything is ready before construction begins.

3. Build & Celebrate

We bring your project to life with clear communication, walkthroughs, and final touch-ups before celebrating your beautifully finished space.

Frequently Asked Questions
Do we have to move out during our remodel?

For a whole-home renovation, you'll likely need to relocate for at least part of the project. Depending on the scope and duration of the project, it may be best if your family moves out of the home completely. This will actually shorten the overall project duration and be more tolerable for you!

If we're looking for a home in a particular neighborhood, can you get us remodel estimates before we purchase?

Yes, if you involve us early in your home search process we can give you general price guidance on specific properties and scopes of work.

Generally, how long does a whole home remodel take?

This can be hard to answer because every remodeling scope is different. If there are no structural changes or additions involved, your project may be done as quickly as four or five months, however for more complicated or comprehensive remodels, timelines can increase up to eight or nine months.

At what point does it make sense to tear down and rebuild instead of taking on a whole home remodel?

A full tear-down can make sense in several situations. (1) The property is in a perfect location with a perfect lot, but the home itself is too small or generally doesn't meet your needs. (2) If there are known structural or health concerns including water damage, mold, or sinking foundations. (3) If your home has experienced a disaster such as fire or flood, it can lend a unique opportunity to start completely fresh with a new layout and functionality for life.

Build the house of your dreams

From design to final inspection our team handles everything. So your custom home build is stress-free.

Start Your Free Consultation
Are you ready for a home you're proud of?

Building a custom home is an opportunity to create a space that is truly designed around the way you live. From the initial vision to the final details, Red Fox Remodeling brings thoughtful design, quality craftsmanship, and a personalized approach to creating a home that is uniquely yours.

Custom Builds Starting at $350k

A custom home can be designed around your lifestyle, your family, and the details that matter most to you. Red Fox Remodeling combines thoughtful planning and quality craftsmanship to help bring your vision to life from the ground up.

Personalized design
No compromising on layout
Built for the future in mind
Modern efficiency & technology
Quality craftsmanship
Here's how it works

We turn your vision into reality with transparency, quality assurance, and customer satisfaction at every step.

1. Discovery & Design

We learn about your vision and budget, create your initial design and estimate, and finalize your project direction through a collaborative design and approval process.

2. Prepare & Plan

Our team handles permits, coordinates partners, and sources all materials to ensure everything is ready before construction begins.

3. Build & Celebrate

We bring your project to life with clear communication, walkthroughs, and final touch-ups before celebrating your beautifully finished space.

Frequently Asked Questions
Do you have a number of set home plans to pick from or do you design from scratch?

We design every home project from the ground up. A custom home is a unique opportunity to leverage every inch of your home to conform to how you want to live. 

Why is a custom home so much more expensive than a new home in a development?

Economies of scale and simplicity of designs. Developers can sell homes for hundreds of thousands less per home because they sell hundreds of homes in a year. Beyond that, generally speaking, homes built by developers take few risks, are simple to construct and use a set number of floor plans. Custom homes are 100% bespoke, include unique and inspiring features, and will only be built once - all those differentiators drive price, but also drive incredible results!

Do you have lots available for building?

We do not currently offer lots for customers to build on. We require custom build customers to secure their own buildable lot and confirm the ability to build with the proper local authorities before purchasing. 

How long does a custom build take from start of design to finish?

Typically a truly custom home will take over a year from the start of design to final inspection. Four to six months are spent locking in the design, with the next eight to ten months spent building the home.

How long does a bathroom remodel take?

A bathroom remodel typically takes 6–8 weeks of construction. Larger primary bathrooms with layout changes, custom tile, or specialty materials can take longer.

Can I live in my home during the remodel?

In most cases, yes, you can continue to live in your home. If your home has more than one bathroom, you can continue living there throughout the project.

How far in advance should I start planning?

Ideally, 3–6 months before you want construction to begin. Specialty materials can have long lead times and it's important to leave time for a full custom design process.

Rec Room. Guest Suite. Cozy Living Space.

Your basement has endless potential. Let’s bring it to life! Whether you’re dreaming of a cozy family hangout, a home office, or a full guest suite, our team specializes in basement refinishing that make every square foot count.

Basements Starting at $95k

With each project thoughtfully designed around how you want to live, entertain, and use your space. We provide transparent pricing throughout the process, so you can confidently plan your investment from design through completion.

Add valuable living space
Increase home value

Here's How it Works.

We turn your vision into reality with transparency, quality assurance, and customer satisfaction at every step.

1. Discovery & Design

We learn about your vision and budget, create your initial design and estimate, and finalize your project direction through a collaborative design and approval process.

2. Prepare & Plan

Our team handles permits, coordinates partners, and sources all materials to ensure everything is ready before construction begins.

3. Build & Celebrate

We bring your project to life with clear communication, walkthroughs, and final touch-ups before celebrating your beautifully finished space.

Frequently Asked Questions
How much will our project cost?

So many factors go into the final construction bid that there is truly no 'one size fits all' answer here. However, for a full basement remodel which includes a bathroom, bedroom and living space, we tend to see project costs around $100,000. 

How long will this project take?

Designing your space with you and making all material selections can take 1-2 months. Once we've finalized the design, the construction phase will be 3-4 months depending on features you've selected and complexity of the project.

How soon can you start our project?

Design can always always start immediately, but our construction start times vary depending on the scope of the work. Typically you could expect to start your project within 4-5 months of signing your design contract.

Do I need drain tile and a sump pump before finishing my basement?

Drain tile is a building system designed to keep groundwater out of your basement and protects your interior finishes (think drywall, carpet, etc). Not every home needs a drain tile system due to water table depth, soil composition, and history of the home - however, this is something we can evaluate with you during the design process.

Do you remediate mold or asbestos issues?

No. We are not an abatement company which are specifically licensed to remove mold, asbestos or other harmful material. However, not all situations require abatement. We can encapsulate asbestos material (leave it in place and install a new product over the top) and many mold problems never rise to the level of needing professional abatement help.

Executive Craftsman

St. Paul

Kitchen • Bathrooms • Primary Bedroom

This young family loved their historic St. Paul home and the character of their established neighborhood, but their growing family had quickly outgrown the home’s compact footprint. With the dining room doubling as overflow kitchen space, no main-level bathroom, and no connection to the backyard, they needed more room without giving up the home and community they loved.
The Client's Needs

The goal was to create a home that felt spacious, functional, and welcoming for the entire family while preserving the historic character that made the original home so special.

Our Design Priorities
1
Expand Without Losing Character

Create a thoughtful addition that feels original to the home by carrying its historic materials, details, and proportions throughout the new spaces.

2
Create Space for Everyone

Give the family dedicated places to cook, gather, work, and relax while creating a better sense of connection between the kitchen, backyard, and rest of the home.

3
Make Every Square Foot Count

Use intentional layouts and carefully selected details to add meaningful function. Even within the home’s smallest spaces.

Kitchen

The new kitchen was designed around the way the family actually lives, with both an island and peninsula providing distinct areas for food preparation, homework, gathering, and everyday seating. A new sliding door creates direct access to the backyard and patio, while hardwood flooring and custom millwork were carefully matched to the original home so the new space feels as though it has always been there.

Half Bathroom

Though the footprint was exceptionally small, the new main-level powder room proves that a compact space can still have plenty of character. Heated floors, wainscoting, and a refined wall-mounted sink make this practical addition feel polished and intentional while giving the family a much-needed bathroom for everyday life and entertaining.

Primary Suite

Upstairs, the new primary suite provides the family with a dedicated retreat, including a sophisticated full bathroom designed for both beauty and improved function. Real marble flooring, an elevated herringbone shower, a reconfigured vanity and toilet layout, and added linen storage turn the compact space into a thoughtful and luxurious upgrade.

Exterior Addition

The rear addition was carefully designed to disappear into the original architecture of the home. Matching the existing siding, windows, and roofing materials created a seamless transition, while the new connection to the patio finally gave the family the backyard access they had been missing.

A note from the owner,

"This was one of those projects where we genuinely loved the people as much as we loved the work. The family was so much fun to work with, and it was incredibly rewarding to help them create a home that could truly accommodate everyone while still honoring the history of the house. We especially loved the challenge of carrying the original home’s historic details into every part of the addition. Most of all, it was exciting to see this family gain the space and functionality they needed without having to leave the home and neighborhood they loved."

​

- Denny Meints

Sophisticated  Living

St. Paul

Kitchen • Bathrooms • Primary Bedroom

This young family loved their St. Paul neighborhood and historic home, but over time, the spaces at the heart of their daily life no longer felt like a reflection of their family or their personal style. With growing children and a desire to stay in their home for years to come, they wanted to create spaces that felt elevated and beautiful while also working better for the way their family actually lived.
The Client's Needs

The goal was to refresh the home’s most-used spaces with a sophisticated, timeless aesthetic while adding practical function for a growing family and honoring the character of the historic home.

Our Design Priorities
1
Elevate the Everyday

Transform the kitchen and bathrooms into beautiful, intentional spaces using natural, high-quality materials that would feel special every day and stand the test of time.

2
Design for Family Life

Improve the function of the home with thoughtful storage, flexible bathing spaces, and layouts that allow multiple family members to use the spaces comfortably at once.

3
Honor the Character

Create a cohesive aesthetic that feels appropriate to the historic house while introducing the family’s more refined, sophisticated style throughout the spaces.

Kitchen

The kitchen became a true focal point of the home with custom walnut cabinetry, polished brass hardware, a solid marble countertop, and a classic farmhouse sink. While the existing layout did not require major functional changes, the transformation of the materials and finishes completely elevated the space, giving the family a kitchen that felt distinctly their own and built to last.

Basement Bathroom

Designed with a more masculine aesthetic for the husband, this basement bathroom balances deep, high-contrast finishes with lighter elements that help brighten the naturally darker space. Brass accents, distinctive floor tile, and added storage give the room both personality and practicality, creating a space that works especially well as a post-workout retreat.

Family Bathroom

The main family bathroom was designed around the realities of life with children, with a dedicated wet room that places the tub and shower together behind glass for contained, easy-to-manage bathing. A curved wall subtly conceals the shower while adding an architectural element, while the combination of a darker wood vanity, marble, brass, and soft finishes creates a timeless and sophisticated look.

A note from the owner,

"What I loved most about this project was that we were able to touch every level of the home and make a meaningful difference in the way this family lives. From the basement bathroom to the main family spaces, every improvement was connected to making their home more functional, more beautiful, and more reflective of who they are. I especially enjoyed finding that balance between sophisticated design and the realities of raising a family, because the spaces still needed to work hard every day. They were also such genuinely kind people to work with, which made the entire project that much more rewarding."

​

- Denny Meints

Garden Cottage 

St. Paul

Kitchen • Bathroom • Dining

This growing St. Paul family loved the history and charm of their home, but a poorly executed renovation in the 1990s had left many of its spaces feeling disconnected, dated, and in need of repair. With a third child on the way and a love for hosting family and friends, they knew it was time to restore the home’s character while making it work better for the life they were building there.
The Client's Needs

The goal was to bring the historic home back to its original character while improving functionality, increasing storage and natural light, and creating a better connection to the garden and outdoors.

Our Design Priorities
1
Restore Historic Character

Reintroduce thoughtful materials, millwork, and architectural details that feel authentic to the home and restore the charm that had been lost over time.

2
Utilize Small Spaces

Reconfigure tight and unconventional spaces with creative layouts, custom features, and purposeful storage so every square foot could serve the family well.

3
Bring the Outdoors In

Increase natural light and strengthen the connection to the family’s beloved garden through new windows, thoughtful sightlines, and nature-inspired colors and materials.

Kitchen

The kitchen was completely reimagined with custom cabinetry, butcher block countertops, brick flooring, handmade backsplash tile, and brass hardware that reinforce the home’s historic character. The layout was carefully rearranged to better accommodate the appliances and daily workflow, while custom features, including a concealed coffee bar behind French-style doors and a hidden bookshelf that opens to reveal basement access, add layers of personality and surprise.

Dining Room

Because hosting was such an important part of this family’s life, the dining room was designed to provide flexibility between everyday living and entertaining. A widened opening with custom doors allows the dining room to open up when they need more gathering space or close off when desired, with custom trim and millwork carefully matched to the historic character of the home.

Bathroom

Working within an exceptionally tight footprint, the bathroom required a creative approach to make every inch functional. A tucked-away vanity, pocket door, wall-mounted toilet, and wet-room configuration allow the shower and toilet to share the compact space, while green tile, a mirrored pocket door, and a window within the shower bring in personality and natural light.

A note from the owner,

"What I loved most about this project was all of the little details that made the home feel completely unique to this family. The hidden basement door, concealed coffee bar, beautiful green accents, and thoughtful connection to their garden each added something special without taking away from the home’s historic character. I especially loved how we were able to bring more natural light and the family’s love of plants into the design, creating spaces that feel both charming and connected to the outdoors. In the end, the home became cozy, functional, and full of character. A place this family can enjoy and cherish for generations."

​

- Denny Meints

Emerald Retreat

St. Paul

Bathroom • Laundry

This family loved their beautiful historic neighborhood and had no desire to leave, but their home’s existing layout created one major everyday frustration: doing laundry meant traveling nearly two full stories. Their primary bathroom also needed a thoughtful update, creating an opportunity to solve the laundry challenge while transforming the space into a bright, elevated retreat that felt worthy of the historic home.
The Client's Needs

The goal was to modernize the primary bathroom, introduce convenient laundry without sacrificing the room’s character, and make the challenging pitched-ceiling layout feel intentional, bright, and luxurious.

Our Design Priorities
1
Maximize Every Inch

Use every inch of the unusual pitched-ceiling footprint to accommodate both a beautiful bathroom and a concealed laundry area without compromising the room’s flow.

2
Bring in Natural Light

Take advantage of the roofline with a strategically placed skylight and integrated lighting to make the space feel open, bright, and connected to the outdoors.

3
Create an Timeless Space

Use classic materials, thoughtful proportions, and refined details to create a bathroom that feels elevated today and beautiful for years to come.

Bathroom & Laundry

The pitched ceiling became an opportunity rather than a limitation, allowing the walk-in shower to tuck naturally beneath the slope with adding a beautiful skylight positioned directly above it. Emerald green tile, marble flooring, heated floors, and integrated lighting around the skylight create a sophisticated, spa-like atmosphere, while the laundry unit is cleverly concealed behind custom French-style cabinetry beside the shower. The cabinetry was crafted by the client’s father, adding an incredibly personal layer of craftsmanship and creating a meaningful heirloom element within the space.

A note from the owner,

"One of my favorite things about this project is how the natural light completely changes the experience of the room. It almost feels like a luxurious treehouse. The skylight, emerald tile, and connection to the outdoors make it such a unique and peaceful space, while the hidden laundry adds an incredible amount of everyday function. But what makes this project especially meaningful is the cabinetry made by the client’s father; knowing that his craftsmanship will remain in the home as an heirloom piece for the family makes the space feel so much more personal. It was incredibly rewarding to take a challenging layout and turn it into something beautiful, functional, and deeply connected to the people who live there."

​

- Denny Meints
